Bachelor's degree in finance, accounting, economics, business administration, or a related field and/or equivalent experience or training.

The Financial Analyst 2 plays an integral role within the Division of Undergraduate Education Finance team, providing comprehensive financial support to an assigned portfolio of divisional units while also supporting senior financial analysts in managing broader divisional financial activities. Under the general direction of senior finance staff, this position applies established financial concepts, University policies, and analytical methods to assignments of moderate scope and complexity. The Financial Analyst 2 supports annual budgeting, financial forecasting, monthly and year-end reporting, variance analysis, position and compensation tracking, transaction review, financial reconciliations, and other financial management activities. This position works closely with finance colleagues, program managers, unit leaders, and other campus partners to maintain accurate financial information, identify and investigate variances, support financial planning, and provide timely and useful financial information to stakeholders.
Financial Planning, Budgeting & Forecasting - 25%
Supports the annual budget and periodic forecasting processes for assigned units, programs, funds, and activities.
Assists in developing revenue and expenditure projections using historical results, current spending patterns, staffing information, known commitments, and established planning assumptions.
Maintains budget and forecast schedules and ensures that supporting documentation is complete, accurate, and current.
Updates financial models and planning tools as new information becomes available.
Assists with the preparation of budget submissions, financial schedules, and supporting analyses.
Works with unit and finance colleagues to collect, validate, and organize information needed for budget and forecast updates.
Identifies significant changes from prior forecasts or budgets and assists in researching the underlying drivers.
Financial Analysis & Management Reporting - 25%
Prepares recurring monthly, quarterly, and year-end financial reports and performs budget-to-actual, forecast-to-actual, and year-over-year variance analyses for assigned portfolios.
Reviews financial results to identify significant variances, trends, unusual activity, and potential areas of concern; researches underlying causes and summarizes findings.
Develops financial schedules and analyses that provide stakeholders with clear and useful information regarding financial performance and available resources.
Supports ad hoc financial analysis and reporting needs for divisional and unit leadership.
Financial Operation and Reconciliations - 20%
Reviews and reconciles financial activity to ensure transactions are accurate, appropriately coded, properly supported, and consistent with University and divisional requirements.
Researches discrepancies and coordinates corrections, journal entries, budget adjustments, funding transfers, and other financial transactions as appropriate.
Tracks commitments, transfers, recharge activity, and other financial obligations to support accurate financial reporting and forecasting.
Supports fiscal year-end close activities, including reviewing outstanding activity, identifying necessary corrections, and ensuring financial records are complete and accurate.
Position & Compensation Financial Management - 15%
Maintains financial tracking for positions, salaries, benefits, vacancies, and staffing changes within assigned units.
Updates salary and benefit projections for new hires, vacancies, changes in appointment, salary adjustments, and other personnel actions.
Reconciles position and compensation information with financial plans and actual expenditures and investigates discrepancies as needed.
Assists in evaluating the financial impact of proposed staffing actions and incorporates approved changes into budgets and forecasts.
Financial Partnership & Customer Service - 5%
Serves as a financial resource for assigned units and develops an understanding of their programs, funding sources, business cycles, and financial needs.
Responds to financial questions, assists stakeholders in interpreting reports, and researches transactions and other financial issues.

Communicates financial information clearly to stakeholders with varying levels of financial knowledge and works collaboratively with unit and campus partners to resolve issues. Identifies matters requiring additional review and appropriately escalates complex, sensitive, or unusual financial issues to senior finance staff.
Financial Compliance and Internal Controls - 5%
Ensures that the appropriate internal controls and financial policies are addressed, maintained and strengthened to protect University resources.
Communicates business and finance policies to unit leadership and staff as needed.
Process Improvement & Special Projects - 5%
Identifies opportunities to improve financial reporting, tracking, reconciliations, documentation, and routine business processes.
Assists with maintaining financial procedures, templates, calendars, and other tools that promote consistency and efficiency across the finance function.
Participates in divisional finance initiatives, data clean-up efforts, system or process improvements, and other special projects as assigned.
Working knowledge of financial analysis, budgeting, accounting, and financial reporting concepts.
Familiarity with current UC financial, reporting, budgeting and human resources systems and/or the ability to learn.
Ability to analyze financial information, identify discrepancies and trends, investigate underlying causes, and summarize findings clearly.
Familiarity with UC business and accounting policies, procedures, chart of accounts, etc. and/or the ability to learn.
Demonstrated ability to effectively present information verbally and in writing clearly and concisely.
Proficiency with spreadsheet applications, including the ability to organize, analyze, reconcile, and present financial data using Microsoft Excel or comparable tools.
Demonstrated interpersonal skills at all levels within an organization; excellent service orientation and critical thinking skills; and attention to detail.
Ability to organize and manage multiple assignments, establish priorities, meet deadlines, and follow through on outstanding items.
Ability to work effectively in a diverse environment and contribute to an inclusive and collaborative workplace.
Intermediate knowledge and understanding of internal control practices and their impact on protecting University resources.
Demonstrated commitment to responsible stewardship of University resources and to maintaining high standards of integrity and accountability.
Strong quantitative and analytical skills with demonstrated attention to accuracy and detail.
